why: The batteries are a circular queue with ready times: simulate battery by battery, each time recording when the depleted one will be ready, and search forward cyclically for the next ready battery. The hint O(t * n) bound tells you a direct simulation is intended.
hints: Track, per battery, the time at which it is usable again. What happens at each moment a battery runs out?
When battery cur depletes at time T, count it, set ready[cur] = T + recharge[cur], then scan cur+1, cur+2, ... (cyclically, at most n batteries) for one with ready <= T. None found means -1.
Stop when the current battery would run past t: that usage is not complete and is not counted. At most t switches, each O(n): O(t * n).
pitfalls: A battery whose charge lasts beyond t does not count; one that runs out exactly at t does.
A battery that becomes ready exactly when needed (ready == now) can be used.
The battery that just died is checked last in the cyclic scan and only works if its recharge is 0.
constraints:
• 1 <= t <= 10^5 (not stated in the source; the stated O(t * n) budget implies a small t)
  • 1 <= capacity.length = recharge.length <= 100 (not stated in the source)
  • 1 <= capacity[i] <= t, 0 <= recharge[i] <= 10^5 (not stated in the source)
